latest_release.name: HMM frozen model v1
latest_release.body:
Portable frozen HMM router artifact for the companion policy sidecar.

- Model: `hmm-router-frozen-v1`
- Embedding contract: `google/gemini-embedding-2`, 3072 dimensions
- SHA-256: `b326bda644aac86831bae47d0b69de008046f62324a4b93a1eba702581c174df`
- Runtime data only: no Python pickle, training rows, prompts, training provenance, or WorkWeave registry dependency

This prerelease is intended for the self-hostable HMM sidecar PR. The router remains on cluster routing unless HMM is explicitly configured.

# Weave Router Weave Router is a proxy that selects a model for each API request. It works with Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini APIs, so you can use it with coding tools or your own application. You can use the hosted router or run it yourself with your own provider keys. For the best experience, use the managed router hosted by Weave. The router uses an embedding and a cluster scorer to choose from enabled models. It supports streaming, tool calls, and vision. The scorer is based on [Avengers-Pro](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.12631). ## Get started For the hosted router, run the installer and follow the setup prompts: ```bash npx @weave-os/router ``` You'll need Node 18 or later. The hosted setup page can help you get a router key; you can also create one in the [Weave dashboard](https://app.weaveos.com/) under Settings → API keys. To choose a tool directly, use one of these commands: ```bash npx @weave-os/router --claude npx @weave-os/router --codex npx @weave-os/router --copilot npx @weave-os/router --opencode npx @weave-os/router --pi ``` The installer configures your selected tool to use Weave. For Copilot, it adds Weave Router to the model picker; you can also start it with `copilot --model weave/auto`. For example, to switch Codex back to its previous provider, run `npx @weave-os/router off --codex`. Use `on --codex` to switch back to Weave, or `--uninstall --codex` to remove the configuration. See the [installation guide](install/README.md) for what changes for each tool, project-level setup, and all available options. For client-specific setup, connection checks, switching back, and uninstall, see the [Router quickstart](https://weaveos.com/router/quickstart), [Claude Code guide](https://weaveos.com/router/claude-code), and [Codex CLI guide](https://weaveos.com/router/codex). ## Run it yourself You'll need Docker, Go 1.26 or later, a provider API key, and a local checkout. For example, with an OpenRouter key: ```bash git clone https://github.com/weave-os/router.git cd router echo 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-...' >> .env.local echo 'ROUTER_ADMIN_PASSWORD=replace-with-a-strong-password' >> .env.local make full-setup ``` This starts the router and Postgres, creates a router key, and offers to set up Claude Code. The router listens at and the dashboard is at . The router key (`rk_...`) is printed during setup; use it to authenticate clients. Your provider key is separate and stays in `.env.local`. Without an admin password, inference still works but dashboard administration is disabled. To connect another supported tool to the local router, add `--local` to its installer command, for example: ```bash npx @weave-os/router --codex --local ``` Cursor routes its Agent and Ask chats through the router. Cursor calls the base URL from its own servers, not from your machine, so a `localhost` router is unreachable: use the hosted router or a publicly reachable self-hosted URL. In Cursor, open Settings → Models, turn on *OpenAI API Key* with your `rk_...` router key, set *Override OpenAI Base URL* to `/v1`, and add a custom model named `weave-auto` (the router rejects other `weave-` names). Tab completion and Apply stay on Cursor's own models, and BYOK needs a paid Cursor seat. The self-hosted router sends prompts to your configured provider. It also supports OpenTelemetry for tracing. For configuration, deployment details, and other provider options, see the [configuration reference](docs/CONFIGURATION.md). ### Self-hosted HMM The optional self-hosted HMM is a barebones, frozen version of the policy. It doesn't include the managed service's training, online learning, or registry. For the best experience, use the [Weave-managed router](#get-started). The self-hosted stack defaults to the cluster scorer; starting the HMM sidecar does not change that default. See the [HMM guide](sidecars/hmm/README.md) for setup and how to select it. ### Architecture The router, cluster scorer, database, and dashboard run locally. Requests go from the router to your configured model provider; you can also send traces to an OpenTelemetry collector. The optional HMM sidecar uses a compatible embedding service; its default configuration calls Google's embedding API. ```mermaid flowchart LR client["Claude Code, Codex, opencode,
pi, Cursor, your own app"] router["Router :8080
/v1/messages · /v1/chat/completions
/v1beta/models · /v1/route"] scorer["Cluster scorer
in-process ONNX embedder"] hmm["HMM policy sidecar :8093
optional, make up-hmm"] pg[("Postgres
installations, rk_ keys,
encrypted BYOK keys, usage")] ui["Dashboard /ui
selfhosted mode only"] providers["Anthropic · OpenAI · Gemini
OpenRouter and any
OpenAI-compatible endpoint"] otel["Your OTLP collector
Honeycomb, Datadog, Grafana"] client -->|"rk_… bearer token,
streamed response back"| router router -->|"embed and score the action"| scorer router -.->|"ROUTER_DEFAULT_STRATEGY=hmm"| hmm router -->|"auth, config, usage"| pg pg --> ui router -->|"provider key from env or BYOK"| providers router -.->|"spans and usage logs"| otel classDef external fill:#f4f4f5,stroke:#a1a1aa,color:#3f3f46 class providers,otel external ``` Multi-replica deployments also need Pub/Sub for cache invalidation; Docker Compose runs an emulator locally. ## API The router accepts Anthropic Messages (`/v1/messages`), OpenAI Chat Completions (`/v1/chat/completions`), and Gemini requests (`/v1beta/models/:action`). To inspect a routing decision without sending a request to a model, use `POST /v1/route`. The [endpoint reference](docs/ENDPOINTS.md) covers health checks, response costs, and the other endpoints. For example, using the local router: ```bash curl http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer rk_...' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hi"}]}' ``` See the [configuration reference](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) for router settings, the [analytics guide](docs/ANALYTICS_EXPORT.md) for exporting routing decisions, and the [session cost guide](docs/SESSION_COST.md) for usage and savings. For the rest of the documentation, including routing terminology and policy integration, see the [documentation index](docs/README.md). ## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development setup and tests. The [architecture guide](AGENTS.md) describes the package layout and the [benchmark guide](bench/README.md) covers the evaluation harness. ## License [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). See [NOTICE](NOTICE) and [THIRD_PARTY.md](THIRD_PARTY.md) for attribution and third-party licenses.
